references.text: Moses sets up a tent of meeting outside the camp as a place for God's presence, parallel to Peter's desire to set up tents for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.
Moses enters the cloud on Mount Sinai, which resembles the cloud that covers Jesus, Moses, and Elijah during the transfiguration.
Elijah meets God on Mount Horeb, where God passes by and speaks to him, reflecting the presence of Elijah and Moses with Jesus.
Isaiah sees the Lord's glory and the seraphim calling to one another, which may recall the divine revelation at the transfiguration.
Matthew's account of the transfiguration, which is a parallel event to Mark 9:5.
Luke's version of the transfiguration, which gives a parallel description to Mark 9:5.
John describes the Word who became flesh and pitched his tent among us, which can be seen as a spiritual parallel to Peter's desire to build tents.
